correctness.rationale: Independently parametrize fixed points by their intracavity phase φ: z=(1−u exp(iφ))⁻¹, with t=1+u²−2u cos φ>0 and κ congruent to K(φ)=φ+η t/(1+t) mod 2π. Distinct phases modulo 2π give distinct points since u>0. The lift has K′(φ)=1+2uη sin φ/(1+t)². Thus uniform strict increase holds for |η| below min_t M_u(t) with M_u as in the record. Its derivative has sign of 8u²−v²−(2+u²)v, v=1+u²−t; evaluation at v=−2u,0,2u locates the only in-domain root at v_*, with the other root below −2u. Divergence of M_u at both endpoints and the derivative signs give the explicit minimum. The lift shifts by 2π across each period, so below the threshold it has exactly one preimage modulo 2π. Above it the sine sign opposite to η at t_* gives K′<0. Choose a level strictly between the lift values at the endpoints of a short decreasing interval; besides the preimage inside, K(φ)−φ bounded gives one to the left and one to the right. They cannot be congruent modulo 2π since they map to the same real level. This proves the symmetric sharp result including all offsets in the uniqueness regime. Independent numerical substitution agrees with all three stated E values.
residual_risks: The frozen claim leaves equality open and does not claim stability or attraction. A finite numerical root scan is not used as a multiplicity proof.

value.rationale: An exact offset-uniform transition distinguishes inability to produce multiple equilibria anywhere in phase space from guaranteed achievable multiplicity at each stronger nonlinearity. It materially sharpens contraction-based uniqueness and provides a parameter/phase construction rather than a plot or one instance. This is a natural boundary of the original map, irrespective of dynamical stability.
